newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly lower.

text.p: Swiss shares closed marginally easier, but held nearly all of Wednesday's strong gains, and traders said an easier U.S. dollar and a slump in Bunds put some pressure on Swiss share prices.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index dipped 2.2 points, or 0.04 percent, to 5,176.4 and the broad Swiss Performance Index was down 1.55 points, or 0.05 percent, to 3,266.80.
Total bourse turnover stood at 2.41 billion francs.
The bank sector lost some of its recent drive, but still outperformed the market.
UBS, which led the actives list, added one franc to 1,524. CS Group continued its recent strong showing, added 2.75 francs to 182.50. But SBC lost ground.
CS Group said after the bourse close that German Siemens will pay 285 francs per share for the bank group's Elektrowatt stake.
Both CS Group and Elektrowatt shares have soared recently after CS confirmed that tax problems associated with the sale of Elektrowatt's industrial business to Siemens had been solved.
Swiss Re was up 49 francs to 1,955 on recommendations.
Pharmaceuticals were under slight pressure after a period of strong gains. Roche certificates slid 140 francs to 13,280. Novartis gave up four francs to end at 2,014.
Nestle fell 18 francs, or nearly one percent, to 1,807. Rising coffee prices were seen as one reason behind the share price decline.
Insurer Baloise rose 20 francs to 3,270 after the company said it expected a rise in 1997 net profit.
